The namespace terminating during test setup is super strange but seems like a test-only issue, not an issue with the functionality being tested. does this help @liggitt ?

feels like a test only problem like @liggitt said. We don't even have gluster in our CI/prow to test against...

cc @msau42 @xing-yang 

Michelle, Xing, Can you please confirm that this is not a blocker for 1.19.0?

Knowing the timeframe for when the test started and when that delete happened would be interesting to know. Possibilities I can see:
* something in the test timed out, and the cleanup happened in parallel with something in the test attempting to run
* multiple tests are reusing the same test context and namespace name at the same time (I can never keep straight how ginkgo parallel tests work)
@dims This does not look like a blocker for 1.19.0.

Thanks @xing-yang!

/milestone v1.20
@liggitt looking at the logs it seems to be the latter "same test context and namespace name at the same time", but we can deal with this for 1.19.1

cc @gnufied @Jiawei0227 
This looks like another instance of "the same test namespace is being reused". I believe @Jiawei0227 had a mitigation for that to try to make the namespaces more unique.
(btw, the test brings up a containerized gluster server so we are exercising gluster functionality)

Yeah, looking at the build log found that it is the same issue as #93749 
The issue is still around the double deletion of namespace, i.e. we delete the test namespace during the test execution, but later on the `AfterEach` call we delete the namespace again to ensure it truly get cleaned up. But unfortunately, this namespace has been reused by another test case between this gap.

Some potential fix I can think of:
1. Since deletion of the primary namespace twice is inevitable, maybe we should consider generate primary namespace based on a hashing of the test cases name?
2. Extends the 4 digits random namespace to 6, this should not solve the problem in nature but it will extremely decrease the chance it happens.
3. Consider using an in-memory namespace map to keep record of already generated namespaces for the whole test run and refuse to generate the same namespace again in the whole lifecycle of a prow job.
@Jiawei0227 do you know if this gluster test is using your mitigation in #93869?

1. A hash of the testcase name + random suffix (because tests can be run multiple times) seems like a good way to mitigate the chances of tests reusing the same namespace. I'm unsure if we know the test case name at the time of test namespace creation though.

2. Otherwise I think increasing the length of the random suffix is a quick and easy mitigation

3. I believe ginkgo [spawns multiple processes](https://onsi.github.io/ginkgo/#parallel-specs) to run in parallel, so this may not work
Yes it is. But my fix in #93869 can only reduce the chance of collision and probably improve readability of logs. But not to eliminate this issue in nature.

AFAICT https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93869 does not affect intree code at all, because it only fixes namespace of driver.  If we are seeing collision of primary namespace for intree code then it is a different problem.

1. Fix on #93869 only deals with the collision between test namespace and driver namespace. And that fix is taking affect.
2. This failure is because a test namespace collides with another test namespace. And this is not related to in-tree code at all. Any test could potentially become flaky because their namespace can be deleted during test execution. It's just happens to be this intree test this time. The root cause for this problem is: 

We cleaned up the test namespace twice which gives it a small gap that another testcase can generate the same namespace and be affected by the second namespace deletion from the original testcase.

/assign 

I would like to give it a shot.
I've opened #94247 to address this issue.

/unassign

/assign @gnufied

review_comments: Should we log a message and simply return if `err != nil && apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` is true?
we still need to remove it from `f.namespacesToDelete` array if `IsNotFound` is true right?
Hmm, I am wondering is it possible another test that has the same namespace getting created between the gap. And by remove that namespace from namespacesToDelete, we are leaking resources?
same comment as below (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94318#discussion_r479613474) , ginko/k8s runs tests parallely in different processes not in different goroutines.
Modifying `f.namespacesToDelete` here is likely to race if `Framework.BeforeEach` in another goroutine is creating namespace by calling `Framework.CreateNamespace()`.
The parallelization in ginkgo/k8s is achieved via processes. i.e - each test runs in its own process, so there is no chance that `f.namespacesToDelete` will be shared between tests.
